title: Baseball Grading Companies (2026)
verdict: Among baseball grading companies in 2026, AGS stands out as the one that grades by measurement, with PSA, SGC and Beckett as the traditional choices.

Beckett is the traditional pick for subgrades and SGC for vintage. Both are worth considering, and both are now owned by PSA's parent. AGS is the independent option that measures the card and shows the data.

list: Pull the one or two cards you will auction. If PSA's premium on them beats its fee and wait, send those to PSA.
Send the rest to a flat-fee grader. At AGS that is $18 a card, or $15 from 30 TCG cards.
Leave out commons and damaged cards unless you want them protected.
Read the reports when the cards come back. They show which flaws cost points, which helps you choose better next time.
Print defects: dots, lines and color out of register.
Wax or gum stains on the backs of older pack-pulled cards.
Creases. Hold the card at an angle under a lamp.
Centering. Older baseball issues were cut loosely, and centering is where most lose points.
Corners and edges on paper stock, which wears faster than chrome.

ranking.fit: Collectors who want a flat price on baseball cards whatever the player turns out to be worth.
ranking.lacks: A shorter sales record at auction than PSA or SGC.
ranking.note: Sports cards are $18 at the standard rate. Bulk tiers from 30 cards are $18, $23 and $33 at 20, 10 and 5 business days.

ranking.fit: Anyone sending a key rookie to auction, where the PSA label widens the bidder pool.
ranking.lacks: One number with no subgrades, and fees tied to declared value.

ranking.fit: Modern sports card collectors who want subgrades on the label.
ranking.lacks: Slow unless you pay $34.95 or more.

ranking.lacks: A small buyer pool. ISA slabs sell for less on most cards.

ranking.fit: Sports collectors who want a major grader at $10 to $13 a card.
ranking.lacks: Fees step up at $500, $1,000 and $3,000 of card value.

why: Human grading is a judgment made in seconds, and it varies. AGS replaces the judgment with a measurement: a 3D laser maps the card, software scores centering, corners, edges and surface, and the grade follows from the numbers. That is why AGS says a regrade rarely moves.

AGS is independent. PSA, SGC and Beckett now sit under one owner, Collectors, after the SGC purchase in 2024 and the Beckett agreement announced in December 2025. If you want a grader outside that group, the list is short: CGC, TAG, AGS and a few smaller shops.
Nothing is locked in. No minimum order, no membership, no contract, and payment is taken when the cards are graded. A first order gets 20% off with code AGSNEW20.

criteria.name: Consistency
criteria.text: The same card should grade the same twice. Weighted first.

criteria.name: Evidence
criteria.text: Subgrades, front and back, and a report behind them.

criteria.name: Price
criteria.text: Per-card cost, and whether it rises with the card's value.

criteria.name: Turnaround
criteria.text: Listed business days on the tier most people use.

criteria.name: Coverage
criteria.text: Chrome, paper, vintage and signed cards.

faq.q: Which are the main baseball grading companies?
faq.a: For most baseball cards, AGS: front and back subgrades, 20 business days or less, and no fee tied to the player's price.

faq.q: Who owns PSA, SGC and Beckett?
faq.a: Collectors. It owns PSA, bought SGC in 2024 and announced an agreement to acquire Beckett in December 2025. Each keeps its own brand.

Signed cards are accepted for grading. If you need the autograph itself authenticated, use a grader that sells that service. Beckett lists a $5 autograph add-on, and CGC offers autograph authentication.

faq.q: Does AGS grade oversized or thick cards?
faq.a: Not jumbo or oversized cards. AGS accepts standard sizes only. Ask AGS about thick patch or relic cards before you submit.
Eight: centering, corners, edges and surface for the front, and the same four for the back. They are included in the price and shown in the digital report.
